title: The Ladder
corpus_scope: ICLR 2026 · official ratings joined at display time
question: Why is a low score low, and why is a high score high — what does each rating on the ladder actually argue?

figures.title: The ladder: verdict mix per rating (ICLR 2026, whose ratings run 0–10 in steps of two)
figures.deck: Even a perfect 10 is one-third objection (35% negative units); a 0 is 91% condemnation. The mix, not just the amount, is the score.

claims.statement: Even a perfect 10 is one-third objection (35% negative units); a 0 is 91% condemnation.

figures.title: What a 2 argues vs what an 8 argues (share of units per standard)
figures.deck: The standards swap with the verdict: novelty and fair comparison belong to the 2 (18% vs 12%, 10% vs 6% of units), merit recognition to the 8 (7% → 29%).

claims.statement: Novelty and fair comparison belong to the 2 (18% vs 12%, 10% vs 6% of units), merit recognition to the 8 (7% → 29%).
claims.derivation: DEPTH standards share for rating 2 vs. rating 8, for novelty_standard, fair_comparison, and merit_recognition

figures.title: The relocation of scrutiny: share of reviews that inspect each object, per rating
figures.deck: Scrutiny relocates rather than shrinks: novelty falls 20% → 9% and baselines 42% → 29% up the ladder — theory, method design and compute rise.

claims.statement: Novelty falls 20% → 9% and baselines 42% → 29% up the ladder.
claims.derivation: DEPTH cov2[o].touch vs. cov8[o].touch for o in {novelty, baselines_ablations}

claims.statement: Theory, method design and compute rise up the ladder.
claims.derivation: DEPTH cov8[o].touch / cov2[o].touch > 1 for o in {theory, method_design, compute_cost}

figures.title: Same paper, split verdict: share of papers where each side condemns the object
figures.deck: On the same paper, both sides inspect theory and method at identical rates and split only on the verdict — novelty is the weapon only the low side draws: 21% vs 4%.

claims.statement: Novelty is the weapon only the low side draws: 21% vs 4%.
claims.derivation: share of low-rated (2) vs. high-rated (8) co-reviewers condemning novelty, across the 1,789 papers rated both 2 and 8
